items.stem: What provides most of the energy that powers the water cycle?
items.explanation: Energy from the Sun heats liquid water and powers evaporation, which keeps the whole water cycle moving.

items.stem: What state change happens during evaporation from an exposed water surface?

options.text: Liquid water changes into water vapor
Solid ice changes straight into vapor

items.explanation: Evaporation is liquid water changing into invisible water vapor. Solar energy supplies much of its energy in the water cycle; it does not require boiling or direct sunlight.

items.stem: Plants take up water through roots. Some water evaporates inside leaves and exits as vapor through tiny leaf openings. What is this process?
items.explanation: During transpiration, water moves from roots through the plant, evaporates inside leaves, and exits through tiny leaf openings as water vapor.

items.stem: Moist air cools enough for liquid cloud droplets to form. What happens to some of the water vapor?

options.text: The vapor is heated and expands
The vapor sinks straight into the soil
The vapor condenses into tiny liquid droplets

items.explanation: When moist air cools enough, some water vapor condenses into tiny liquid droplets. Clouds may contain droplets and/or ice crystals; they do not all produce precipitation.

items.stem: Rain, snow, sleet, and hail are all forms of what?
items.explanation: Cloud droplets and/or ice particles can grow large enough to fall as precipitation. Gravity pulls them downward toward land and ocean.

items.stem: After rain falls on a hillside, water flows downhill into streams and rivers. What is this moving surface water called?
items.explanation: Runoff is precipitation that flows across the land surface and collects in streams, rivers, and the ocean.

items.stem: Some rainwater soaks down into the soil and rock instead of flowing across the surface. What is this process called?
items.explanation: Infiltration happens when water soaks down into the soil and rocks below the surface.

items.stem: Water filling saturated pores and fractures in soil and rock is called what?
items.explanation: Groundwater occupies saturated pores and fractures: spaces filled with water. It can stay stored or flow to springs, streams, lakes, and oceans. Some infiltrated water remains in soil instead of reaching groundwater.

items.stem: What force pulls precipitation downward and helps runoff flow downhill?
items.explanation: Gravity pulls precipitation downward and helps runoff flow downhill. Solar energy supplies energy for much evaporation. Gravity acts throughout the Earth system, not just after clouds form.

items.stem: What does it mean that Earth is a closed system for water?

options.text: Every drop must follow the same four stages
Water must return to the ocean before it can evaporate
Water moves and can stay stored within Earth, without being added or removed by the water cycle
Water stays in one reservoir without changing state

items.explanation: Earth is a closed system for water. The water cycle redistributes water among reservoirs within Earth, with state changes and storage along many possible pathways. Closed system does not mean one closed-loop route.
